item.title: “People love this event”: Parallels returns despite funding cut
item.description: Sony President Shuhei Yoshida once heralded the Melbourne showcase as one of his favourite gaming industry events. It’s back, but thanks to a mammoth effort from Freeplay’s board.
item.dc:creator: Jam Walker

item.title: Dredge's Nadia Thorne on her second studio, and what comes next after indie success
item.description: It’s windfall could have seen New Zealand’s Black Salt Games expand, but instead they are looking at self-publishing, spinning out new studios, and curiously, not focusing on horror.
item.dc:creator: James

item.title: The games that got away: Crow Country, Digimon Story: Time Stranger and Yoshi and the Mysterious Book
item.description: Somehow, the easiest game I’ve played in a long while also gave me the most videogame tilt I’ve experienced all year.
item.dc:creator: Harrison Polites

item.title: Indies in the classroom: Ludolio's bid to reshape education with videogames
item.description: And, in turn, provide a “second launch” for titles that may have a place in the curriculum.
item.dc:creator: Harrison Polites

item.title: Virtual chicken noodle soup: The greatest games for your next sick day
item.description: Substack’s gaming community reveals the games that make them feel better when they are down and out.
item.dc:creator: Harrison Polites

item.title: In pictures: The epic booths of Gamescom

item.title: Too many indies, too many creators: Can PlayIndies solve gaming’s discovery dilemma?
item.description: An international startup, with roots in Western Australia, is taking on one of indie gaming’s greatest challenges.
